summary: I sent the exact brief with no visual cues. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and read settings.html/css/js. It then decided on its own to open the visual companion: it ran start-server.sh, gave me a http://localhost:49296/?key=… URL, and wrote layout.html with three mockups (A stacked sections, B card per group, C sidebar/tabs). It asked which one I wanted. I picked B, and it then edited settings.html and settings.css. It wrote no spec, no plan, and no docs/ folder.
reasoning: All 8 criteria have evidence from the session log, the files on disk, or the screen. Without any visual cue in the brief, the agent opened the visual companion when the layout question came up. It kept the design in chat on the bounded path, wrote no spec or plan, asked me to pick a layout before coding, and implemented my pick.

observations.description: The Claude Code startup dialogs for folder trust and the bypass-permissions warning start with the cursor on "No, exit". That's probably intentional as a safe default, but it adds steps to the eval harness flow.

The companion writes its mockups and server state into the repo under .hyperpowers/brainstorm/, which shows up as untracked in git status. The agent pointed this out itself and offered to add a .gitignore entry or delete the folder. Writing these files outside the repo, or adding the ignore entry automatically, might be cleaner.
The agent's companion message says "The tab uses a lot of tokens, so tell me if you'd rather stay in the terminal". Useful, but a bit of an odd thing to tell an end user.

The companion server stays running after the work is done (the agent says it will "shut itself down after 4 hours idle, or I can stop it now"). It didn't stop the server automatically once implementation began.
The agent did not open the result in a browser to check it visually. It said so honestly: "I haven't opened the page in a browser to look at it." It did check that all 12 field names are kept.

criteria.evidence: In the session log, the first tool_use is Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}. It comes before any Edit to public/. The agent's text: "Using brainstorming to shape the settings layout rework."

criteria.criterion: Visual companion opened with localhost URL and HTML screen of candidate layouts
criteria.evidence: Log shows Bash `bash .../skills/brainstorming/scripts/start-server.sh --project-dir ...`, then a Write to .hyperpowers/brainstorm/14761-1790841096/content/layout.html (option cards A/B/C, each with a mockup div). Screen: "I've opened three layout sketches in a browser tab: http://localhost:49296/?key=d4c2b1a3..."

criteria.criterion: Opened just-in-time, not upfront; no non-visual questions sent through the browser
criteria.evidence: Tool order in the log: Skill, git ls-files, cat the settings files, read visual-companion.md, start-server.sh, Write layout.html. The server started only once the layout question came up. It did not announce the companion beforehand. The agent asked no separate scope questions; its question about grouping was asked in the terminal: "If you'd group the fields differently, say so too."

criteria.criterion: Bounded classification held, no ceremony escalation
criteria.evidence: Design stayed in chat: one message offered three options with a recommendation, then implementation started straight after my pick. There were no sectioned design reviews and no spec. The only Skill invocation in the log is brainstorming (grep '"name":"Skill"' returned one hit).

`ls -R docs` returned "No such file or directory". `find coding-agent-workdir -path '*/specs*'` returned nothing. `git status --short` shows only: M public/settings.css, M public/settings.html, ?? .hyperpowers/

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: grep for Skill tool_use found only hyperpowers:brainstorming. The 'writing-plans' matches in the log are only the skill listing and the brainstorming skill's own text. `find ... -name '*plan*.md'` returned nothing.

criteria.criterion: Asked for approval of layout before writing code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Which layout do you want? You can click one in the browser or reply here." The log has no Edit to public/* before my reply "B, the card per group, looks right — go with that."
After my reply the log shows Edit calls on public/settings.html and public/settings.css. Screen: "The settings page now uses option B: each of the four groups sits in its own card..."
